title: Micro-patch audit schema and taxonomy for admin & SAML events
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: RBAC v2 introduces richer role inheritance, SSO/SAML account linking, and multi-step admin flows (canary role rollouts, delegated admin). Current audit outputs are either full snapshots (high bandwidth/storage) or overly verbose raw diffs that are hard to query. Problem: we need a space-efficient, query-friendly event format that captures intent, actor confidence, object context, and a compact field-diff for storage and later reconstruction. Goal: define a lightweight 'micro-patch' event schema and a taxonomy for classifying admin and SSO-related audit events; provide ingestion/retention guidance and console surface mappings. Scope: server-side admin operations, SSO link/unlink, API key & service-account management, role grants/revokes, RBAC policy edits. Not in scope: application-level user activity logs (handled by product teams).
acceptance_criteria: A schema doc exists describing top-level fields, allowed types, and semantics for micro-patch events
Ingestion pipeline accepts micro-patch payloads and validates schema with a test vector suite
Examples cover: role grant/revoke, SSO assertion link, API key creation, delegated admin canary rollout
Event taxonomy (ACCESS|PRIVILEGE|CONFIG|AUTH|SYSTEM) documented and mapped to retention/alerting policies
Actor identity model supports: user, service_account, oauth_client, external_idp with actor_confidence score
Field-diff format reconstructs previous and current resource state using micro-patch application algorithm
Redaction rules defined (PII/credentials) and enforced at ingestion with sampling guidance
Console shows per-event context (actor, target, micro-patch humanized summary) for admin events
Security review completed and KMS encryption for PII-in-logs approved

decision_log: Use micro-patch (field-level change with sparse fields) instead of full snapshots to minimize storage and speed queries
Represent each patch as a list of operations: set, unset, array-add, array-remove, replace; operations are ordered by intent timestamp
Include an explicit intent_tag (e.g., 'role_grant:canary', 'sso:link') to drive alerting and retention decisions
Actor model: capture primary_actor, acting_token (if present), session_id, and actor_confidence (0-100) to reflect SSO assertion mappings
Do not rely on external idp raw assertions in storage; store canonical idp_reference with minimal linkage and index by external_id_hash
Store micro-patch payloads compressed (snappy) and keep an uncompressed sample set for QA and diffs in short-term hot storage
For privacy, redact credential-like fields (api_key, secret, saml_raw_response) at ingestion; keep a schema-level allowlist for diagnostic retention
Adopt state-hash (SHA256) of canonical resource state after applying micro-patches to enable fast reconstruction and integrity checks
examples:
Example: role grant micro-patch event -> {
  "event_type": "PRIVILEGE", 
  "intent_tag": "role_grant:batch", 
  "actor": "user:alice@example.com", 
  "actor_confidence": "98", 
  "target": "org:acct-1234", 
  "patch_ops": "[set roles[+]:'admin']", 
  "metadata": "reason=oncall-rotation;ticket=PM-4821"
}
